plain_english_explanation: Rather than continuing to troubleshoot why manually reflecting ICS differences in the PTS tool wasn't successfully bringing MPS into the test scope, the practical and reliable solution was for Allion to directly share its own already-correctly-configured PTS ICS file (the one used internally for this exact registration, including the necessary profile difference changes) so the customer could load it directly into their own PTS tool and test MPS without needing to replicate the configuration manually.
consultant_answer: Here's our PTS ICS file (attached) — it already has the correct profile difference configuration for this registration, including MPS. decision_logic: When a customer's manual ICS-difference replication approach fails to bring a specific profile into PTS test scope, the most direct and reliable fix is to share the certification lab's own working ICS configuration file rather than continuing to debug the manual replication process.
final_recommendation: When a customer's manual PTS configuration approach is missing a specific profile from test scope, offer to share the lab's own verified ICS configuration file directly as the fastest resolution, rather than spending further time diagnosing the manual replication gap.
risk_if_done_wrong: Continuing to troubleshoot the customer's manual ICS-replication approach indefinitely, rather than simply sharing the working configuration file, would waste time that could otherwise be spent completing the actual MPS retest.
